chunks: Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Maktab (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi told us, saying: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i told us, from his paternal uncle Husayn ibn Yazid, saying: Ali ibn Ghurab told me, saying: The Best of the Ja'fars, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, told me, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father, peace be upon them.
He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Trim the mustaches, leave the beards, and do not resemble the Zoroastrians.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on trimming mustaches and growing beards according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar* with a strong chain of transmission back to the Prophet, this hadith establishes the trimming of mustaches and lengthening of beards as a distinctive Sunnah to differentiate Muslims from the Magians (Zoroastrians) of that era. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on *tashabbuh* (resemblance) as a means of preserving communal identity and following the Prophet’s physical example.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Hussain bin Ibrahim bin Ahmad bin Hisham al-Maktab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Ja’far al-Asadi, that he said: We were told by Musa bin Imran al-Nakha’i, from his paternal uncle, Hussain ibn Yazid, that he said: I was told by Ali bin Ghurab, that he said: I was told by the Best of all named Ja’far, Ja’far bin Muhammed, from his father, from his grandfather, from his gather, peace be upon them, that he said:
The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Trim the mustaches, leave the beards and do not resemble (yourselves with) the Zoroastrians.
